Frontier models like Astra scale autonomous reasoning, but for enterprise adoption, execution authority remains the bottleneck. The next critical layer isn't more probabilistic prompt guardrails on the model level—it's stateless, deterministic verification at the execution layer. Giving enterprise microservices an immutable, hardware-backed approval receipt (Ed25519) ensures frontier intelligence executes with total zero-trust assurance.

Tried it yesterday. In just a few hours I went from copy paste between my AI chat and VSCode to coding without actually touching VSCode at all. It’s does it all, read my repository, find the files it needs to change to achieve my requirement, create backups of the files to edit, edit the files, create a new docker image, push the image to container and restart container without me changing app. I actually tested having Claude opus 5 and GPT 6 astra provide response to the same rei quest and then having Opus and Astra discuss their suggested code and agree on best version for the requirement or propose a new solution to the problem. Opus admits Astra is better in coding. Astra is very very good and very fast to provide responses. Haven’t tested Mythos, curious to compare to Astra.
